Mail-key frequency table for a reference corpus

Source: R/normalize.R
np_mail_freq.Rd

Counts how many reference records share each exact mail_key (box + ZIP). This is what makes a shared box interpretable rather than merely true, and it is not an optional refinement — measured over the 3,687,435-row unified BMF, the key separates two populations that want opposite treatment:

Usage

np_mail_freq(mail_keys)

Arguments

mail_keys

Character vector of mail keys (reference mail_key), as built by np_mail_key(). Empty strings are dropped, so records that name no box do not all pile onto one entry.

Value

A named integer vector mapping mail_key -> record count.

Details

  • A box shared by two or three filers is the signal worth having: an organization and its foundation, a parent and its chapter, a small group of charities run out of one accountant's office. 30,097 of the 36,910 shared boxes hold exactly two EINs and 3,829 hold three.

  • A box shared by hundreds is a service bureau and is evidence of nothing. 678 boxes hold ten or more EINs, and the most crowded — PO BOX 653067 in ZIP 75265 — holds 3,626. Treating that as common administration would link 3,626 unrelated organizations to each other.

So read mail_key as evidence only below a threshold, the same way np_addr_freq()'s share_min gates an address. Overall: 496,830 distinct mail keys, 7.43% of them shared, and 20.79% of box-holding EINs on a shared box.

See also

np_mail_key(), np_addr_freq()
